projects.title: Printit
projects.tagline: From a document to a printed page. Without the chaos.
projects.summary: A cloud printing service connecting customers, print shops, and the unreliable world of physical printers.
projects.problem: Printing a document often means sending files over WhatsApp, repeating instructions, and losing track of the order. Printit brings document preparation, ordering, and fulfillment into one workflow.
projects.contribution: I designed the client, vendor, and backend architecture and built the desktop printing workflow. My work connects user-facing interfaces with cloud orchestration and Windows printing APIs.

decisions.title: Keep the cloud lean
decisions.text: Prepare documents on the client so users control the output before upload. The backend orchestrates data flow; a stateless NestJS service leaves room to scale when demand warrants it.

decisions.title: Make unpredictable hardware manageable
decisions.text: A pure reducer returns the next state and declarative commands. An executor handles IPC, network calls, retries, and printer interactions, then feeds results back as events.

decisions.title: Recover with intent
decisions.text: Persist application state in IndexedDB through Zustand, with rehydration safeguards that reset in-flight queue state. Keep side effects outside the reducer so transitions can be reasoned about independently.

projects.note: Archived independent project, currently dormant and unmaintained. It did not acquire users; the architecture is presented as engineering work, not a production success story.

projects.title: Auction Hub
projects.tagline: A clear contract for every bid.
projects.summary: An auction REST API built around explicit contracts, layered business logic, and stateless authentication.
projects.problem: An auction backend needs a consistent interface for users, items, bids, and auctions. Clients need to know what to expect, while authentication and persistence need clear boundaries.
projects.contribution: I built an API-first Spring Boot service with generated server interfaces, service and repository layers, DTO mapping, and JWT/OAuth2 security.

decisions.title: Start with the contract
decisions.text: Define endpoints in OpenAPI 3 and generate Spring server stubs during the Maven build. Consumers can inspect the same contract used to shape the implementation.

decisions.title: Separate transport from persistence
decisions.text: Use DTOs and MapStruct at the API boundary, with Spring Data JPA and Hibernate for persistence. H2 supports development; MySQL configuration provides an alternative runtime database.

decisions.title: Treat security as a boundary
decisions.text: Use Spring Security with JWT and OAuth2 authentication, rather than scattering authentication logic through business services.

projects.note: Source project; no public hosted demo is claimed.

projects.title: Fable
projects.summary: A library management system with separate experiences for members, librarians, and administrators.
projects.problem: Library members and staff have different needs. Fable separates the member experience from library operations while sharing the data needed to manage books and memberships.
projects.contribution: During my Infosys internship in Mysuru, I worked primarily on the administrator and librarian application as a backend architect and developer. I also served as Scrum Master in a ten-person team.

decisions.title: Design around distinct roles
decisions.text: Separate the member and staff applications, so library operations have an interface suited to administrators and librarians.

decisions.title: Keep views focused
decisions.text: Organize the application using models, services, view models, and SwiftUI views. MVVM creates a place for view state without putting every responsibility into the screen.

decisions.title: Isolate data access
decisions.text: A dedicated Firestore service fetches book metadata asynchronously. Service boundaries keep external data access separate from presentation.

projects.note: Internship team project. Demo videos below show the developed applications.

projects.title: CareNote
projects.role: Medical document scanner developer & project maintainer
projects.tagline: Health information, made easier to navigate.
projects.summary: An early team-built iOS health app exploring medical records, current vitals, and medication workflows.
projects.problem: Health records, vital readings, and medication information are easier to understand when they can be viewed together. CareNote explores that experience in a native iOS app.
projects.contribution: I built the OCR-enabled medical document scanner and maintained the shared project by reviewing and merging teammates’ pull requests. I also collaborated on the prototype design and iOS application.

decisions.title: Prototype the experience first
decisions.text: The team designed health overview and current-vitals screens before translating the UI into the application. The images shown here are design prototypes, not production screenshots.

decisions.title: Turn a document into usable information
decisions.text: I built the scanner using the native Vision text-recognition workflow. The implementation extracts text from medical document images and organizes recognized parameters for the app’s health-record workflow.

decisions.title: Keep team delivery moving
decisions.text: As a project maintainer, I merged contributions from teammates into the shared application. The wider codebase combines UIKit screens with SwiftUI charts; my specific implementation focus was the document scanner.

projects.note: Team-built iOS project. Images are design prototypes; my documented contributions are the OCR scanner and PR maintenance.

projects.title: MyPay
projects.summary: End-to-end work on a website editor and employee system, alongside a major frontend modernization.
projects.problem: New product development and a large legacy application create different engineering challenges. At MyPay, my work spans a visual website editor, an employee management system, and the ongoing modernization of a roughly 200,000-line frontend.
projects.contribution: I own backend and frontend work end-to-end for the website editor and employee management system. On the legacy rewrite, I work mostly on the frontend, with some backend contributions, using AI-assisted development.

decisions.title: Own the workflow across layers
decisions.text: For the website editor and employee system, I work across the backend and frontend rather than owning a single UI slice. The employee management system was designed and created for the company.

decisions.title: Give the frontend explicit boundaries
decisions.text: The modern merchant-portal stack includes React and TypeScript, TanStack Router for navigation, TanStack Query for server state, and React Hook Form with Zod for form validation. These tools separate distinct application concerns.

decisions.title: Make quality checks part of the toolkit
decisions.text: The portal configuration includes TypeScript checks, Biome, Vitest and Testing Library, MSW, and Playwright. Its check script combines type checking, Biome, design-token checks, and unit tests; browser tests have a separate command.

decisions.title: Modernize a large existing surface
decisions.text: The legacy frontend is roughly 200,000 lines. I am helping rewrite it with a modern stack and AI-assisted development. This is ongoing work, not a claim that the migration is complete.

projects.note: Professional work. This overview uses owner-confirmed responsibilities and the provided merchant-portal tooling manifest. Internal source code, screenshots, business metrics, and deployment details are not published here.
